articles.headline: Where is Jaylen Waddle? Broncos' big offseason acquisition is off to slow start
articles.description: With just 204 receiving yards through five games, Jaylen Waddle has been mostly contained and hasn't yet made the impact the Broncos hoped. What has gone wrong?
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ワドルはどこへ？ブロンコスの大型補強選手、出だしは鈍い
articles.descriptionJa: 5試合でレシービングヤードがわずか204ヤードに留まるジェイレン・ワドルは、大半の試合で相手に抑え込まれており、ブロンコスが期待したほどのインパクトを与えられていない。一体何が原因なのか？
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- After a failed third-down conversion Sunday in a game filled with failed third-down plays, Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle stormed into the bench area, ripped his helmet from his head as if it were in flames and slammed its crown into the bench.

It summed up a frustrating day for the receiver, who finished with two receptions for 19 yards in a 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. It marked the third time in five games in which he finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards, and the fourth in which he gained 35 or fewer.

Waddle was by far the Broncos' most significant acquisition in an offseason in which they chose to mostly run it back with a roster that got them to the AFC Championship Game last season. Denver sent first- and third-round picks to the Miami Dolphins to acquire him in March in addition to a fourth-round pick swap. But Waddle, who had 910 receiving yards and six TDs last season, has been rendered ornamental much of the time in an offense that coach Sean Payton said has a long list of problems. And as the 3-2 Broncos get set to host the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-2) on Thursday (8:15 p.m. ET, Empower Field at Mile High, Prime Video), they're trying to figure out how to unleash Waddle.

"I'm watching the film offensively and there are a ton of things we're not doing well right now," Payton said Monday. "So, that has to improve."

Payton was giddy about Waddle's arrival this spring, calling the speed, acceleration, toughness and locker room demeanor of the receiver a "10, 10, 10, 10, 10." Throughout training camp, Waddle flashed his ability to turn any reception into a field-flipping play as a potent vertical threat.

"[That] makes him so tough to play tight," said Broncos All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II, who played with Waddle in college at Alabama. "He can just run by you, or his routes are so clean if you play off, he's going to catch it and turn it into something big."

But the Broncos' offense has been mired in an across-the-board struggle that has eaten into Waddle's production. While Waddle has 18 receptions for 204 receiving yards and a touchdown, much of that came in a Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in which he caught eight passes for 138 receiving yards. His output has been meager otherwise -- a combined 10 receptions for 66 yards in the other four games. Waddle has been targeted an average of 6.2 times per game, a lower rate than he had in four of his five seasons with the Dolphins. That average falls to 5.3 when the Jaguars game is removed.

But there might not be a redder flag in Waddle's lagging production than comparing it to that of backup running back RJ Harvey. Harvey, who has played only 42% of the team's offensive snaps this season and missed one game because of injury, leads the Broncos with 20 receptions.

articles.headline: Chiefs still have faith in pass rush, despite going without a sack since Week 1
articles.description: Entering this week, the Chiefs ranked 27th in pass rush win rate and hadn't recorded a sack since Week 1.
articles.headlineJa: 第1週以来サックなしも、チーフスはパスラッシュへの信頼を維持
articles.descriptionJa: 今週を迎えるにあたり、チーフスのパスラッシュ成功率はリーグ27位に沈んでおり、第1週以来サックを記録できていない。
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Following their bye week, the Kansas City Chiefs returned to the training facility Tuesday, their first day in preparation for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Longtime defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo shared earlier this month that his first meeting with his players on Tuesday often includes him reminding them of where they must improve.

"We like to have constructive criticism," Spagnuolo said then. "The good thing about this group is they're all pretty accountable. Even if I'm standing there and pointing something out, I see a lot of heads are shaking, [saying], 'Yeah, you're right.'"

This week, one of the main areas for the Chiefs defense to address is the unit's lack of a single sack over the past month.

The Chiefs, who are undefeated at 4-0, are hoping that statistical trend ends Sunday against a Chargers team that has struggled to properly protect quarterback Justin Herbert. One reason the Chargers are 0-5 is because Herbert has been sacked at least twice in every game. Without right tackle Joe Alt (neck), left tackle Rashawn Slater (right ankle), left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and backup guard Trevor Penning (concussion), Herbert was sacked five times last week in the Chargers' loss to the Denver Broncos.

Entering this week, the Chiefs ranked 27th in pass rush win rate, generating pressure by beating the opponent's pass protection within 2.5 seconds just 45% of the time. The concern for the Chiefs after their most recent game, a comeback win over the Las Vegas Raiders, is that quarterback Kirk Cousins, who they pressured on just 34.6% of his pass drops, was the least mobile passer they have faced so far this season.

"We've done a good job of keeping the quarterback busy back there, though, with pressure, which is important," coach Andy Reid said Monday. "Hands down, we want to have sacks. But the pressure on the quarterback ends up being an important thing, and I think our guys have been generating that."

In the Chiefs' overtime win against the Indianapolis Colts, quarterback Daniel Jones was able to defeat pressure with quick completions, most of which occurred in the middle of the field. Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis, who was sacked nine times in two games prior to facing the Chiefs, used his legs to escape pressure from pass rushers such as Chris Jones, George Karlaftis and rookie R Mason Thomas.

Against the Raiders, Jones was quick to give his assessment of why Cousins wasn't sacked.

"In order to win, you can't beat yourself," Jones said. "I think a lot of times we've made costly penalties that put us back."

Late in the fourth quarter, Cousins was in the process of trying to get the Raiders to rally from an 11-point deficit. Just before the two-minute warning, Cousins was swarmed in the backfield by Karlaftis, Thomas and defensive end Ashton Gillotte. The problem, however, was that the sack was nullified by a holding penalty from nickel cornerback L'Jarius Sneed.

articles.headline: Is Seahawks OC Brian Fleury a 'home run' hire? How the rookie playcaller is faring
articles.description: Fleury took over the reigns of the Seahawks' Super Bowl champion offense despite never having called plays. How's he doing through five weeks?
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスのOCブライアン・フルーリーは「大当たり」の採用か？新人プレイコーラーの現状
articles.descriptionJa: フルーリーは、プレイコールの経験がないまま、スーパーボウル制覇を成し遂げたシーホークスのオフェンス指揮を執ることになった。開幕から5週間、彼の成績はどうだろうか？
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Sam Darnold has a favorite adjective for first-year Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury: stoic.

"Whether it's a good play or bad play," Darnold said over the summer, "his mentality never changes out there on the field."

That was true even when a wrench was thrown into Fleury's playcalling debut -- his starting quarterback going down on the fifth play of the Seahawks' season opener with what was later determined to be a glute injury.

After taking over for Darnold, backup Drew Lock led five straight scoreless possessions. With the Seahawks trailing by seven early in the fourth quarter, they faced a fourth-and-1 from the New England Patriots' 45-yard line. Fleury put the ball in Lock's hands, dialing up a play-action throw that resulted in a tying touchdown to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. With Darnold watching on his phone from a nearby hospital, Lock led another field goal drive on the ensuing possession, and Seattle's defense sealed a 13-10 win with a third interception of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

Afterward, Lock credited Fleury for providing a calming voice amid the chaos.

"I think as a quarterback, with someone in the headset, you want them [to have the same demeanor] all the time," Lock said. "It was awesome to feel that from him tonight and see that from him and know that's what we're going to get moving forward."

It has become clear what kind of personality Seattle has spearheading the offense. There was never much question as to what the West Coast scheme itself would look like, as it's largely unchanged from the one Klint Kubiak ran before leaving to become the head coach for the Las Vegas Raiders. But there is a question of whether Fleury can pick up where his predecessor left off and coordinate a championship-caliber offense in his first season in that role at any level.

Heading into a Thursday night matchup with the Denver Broncos (3-2) at Empower Field at Mile High (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video), Fleury's offense ranks eighth in scoring at 26.8 points per game. But it's also 25th in expected points added and 26th in ESPN's efficiency metric, indicative of flaws that Seattle's defense and special teams have helped cover.

Those flaws? Too many turnovers and an insufficient run game. Darnold has not taken care of the ball, throwing five interceptions in three games since returning in Week 3. And neither has Seattle's backfield, which also hasn't generated much production on the ground with its top two options -- rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest) and Zach Charbonnet (knee) -- currently sidelined by injuries.

Can a rookie coordinator fix those issues before the Seahawks (3-2) lose any more ground to the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) in the NFC West standings?

articles.headline: Are Panthers positioned to add reinforcements before NFL trade deadline?
articles.description: Armed with draft capital and sitting at 2-2, Carolina has leverage unlike in years past. So what does it mean?
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズはNFLのトレード期限前に戦力を補強できる立場にあるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: ドラフト権を保有し、戦績も2勝2敗のカロライナは、例年とは異なる交渉の優位性を持っている。それが何を意味するのか？
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- The Carolina Panthers come out of their bye week with their best four-game record in five seasons. And at 2-2, the Panthers stand alone at the top of NFC South division race with four weeks until the annual NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

With the Panthers sitting in an unprecedented position under the current front office, Carolina is in an interesting spot when it comes to consideration of midseason reinforcements. While several notable names -- including starting right tackle Taylor Moton (blood clot), starting defensive end Tershawn Wharton (neck) and top returner Trevor Etienne (ankle) -- are expected to make their 2026 debuts in short order, the Panthers could use improved depth at a few positions with injuries piling up. That's where the trade deadline could come into play, and Carolina is inarguably better positioned to add players than in years past, especially if the team finds a good fit on the market.

Panthers general manager Dan Morgan has been methodical about parting with draft capital for incoming players during his tenure, which began in 2024. In fact, his first straight-up trade involving an outgoing pick for an incoming player -- without a player or pick swap -- happened less than two months ago, when Morgan traded a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers in late-August for defensive lineman TeRah Edwards, who played in each of the Panthers' first four games before their Week 5 bye.

The Edwards trade, while a minor deal, shows Morgan isn't going to be stubborn with his draft assets if it means he can upgrade a roster primed for a potential repeat division championship.

Panthers coach Dave Canales said he and Morgan speak about potential roster moves "all the time."

"I won't get into specific positions or anything like that, but Dan has done a great job of trying to look for opportunities that may present themselves to us to be able to challenge our roster in the right way," Canales said Tuesday. "We're always open, we're always looking. I'll pop into his office right after this meeting for about 15 or 20 minutes. And we may be watching [saying], 'Hey, let's take a look at this guy.' We may be watching a college player as he's starting to gather his evaluations, but always having those conversations, to be ready for what could be."

While the Panthers have momentum coming off a Week 4 win against the Detroit Lions and quite a few talented players who are getting healthy, adding external talent could help push the team beyond the standard they set last season with an 8-9 playoff berth.

articles.headline: Sir Gareth Southgate rules out a return to Premier League management
articles.description: Former England head coach Sir Gareth Southgate has said that he doesn't see a scenario where he manages a Premier League club again.
articles.headlineJa: ガレス・サウスゲート卿、プレミアリーグでの監督復帰を否定
articles.descriptionJa: 元イングランド代表監督のガレス・サウスゲート卿は、再びプレミアリーグのクラブを率いるシナリオは考えられないと述べた。
articles.body:
Former England head coach Sir Gareth Southgate has said that he doesn't see a scenario where he manages a Premier League club again.

The ex-Middlesbrough boss has been out of management since the summer of 2024 -- when he led England to another Euros final but resigned after they lost 2-1 to Spain.

Southgate said that he doesn't "see a scenario where I do that" when asked if he would return to Premier League management, in an interview on Amol Rajan's podcast.

"Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying the wins that keep you going. By the end, I didn't enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes," he said.

"I've hardly watched football. I went to the Champions League final the year after I left England, 2025. I went to the FA Cup final to see my team -- Crystal Palace -- win their first trophy. I've not been to a football ground since.

"My desire to be involved in football has changed. I've loved the last 18 months of my life. I've had 37 years where my sense of self depending on 'Did I win? Did I win or lose on Saturday?'

"I've loved having different experiences. I've been curious about what's been going on with young people, I've met politicians, I've met people in the media industry, I've travelled around the world learning things...I've just enjoyed playing a different film in my life."

Recently, Southgate has been heavily involved in the push to understand the mental health struggles that young men and boys face and embarked on a BBC documentary that attempted to encourage them to open up and talk about complex feelings.

"The beauty of England is I was coaching and there was a purpose to it [...] If you go to a club, there's not that same sense of purpose. Do these owners have the values that I have? Can we win? I'm not interested in survival and just being a manager because it's a good salary. That doesn't excite me.

"I'd rather make a bigger difference in my life in other areas than be at one training ground [...] I've given every ounce I had to football and I just fancy a different period of my life."

- Xabi Alonso insists Cole Palmer committed to representing England after Thomas Tuchel dig

- Alex Scott injury not England's fault - Bournemouth boss

Southgate and Rajan also discussed the Manchester City situation. Last month, an independent panel found the club guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules for a number of years.

City have appealed the verdict.

Southgate said there are "no winners" in the City case.

"There will be the tribal fans' response, which is to punish Man City as much as we can, 'relegate them, we missed out because of this.' I've been in football boardrooms and I've been in meetings with UEFA and meetings with FIFA. I've been in these spaces and I know how complicated all of this is," he said.

"My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners."

articles.headline: Mamadou Sangare challenges Brentford to aim for 'top two' Premier League finish
articles.description: Mamadou Sangare has challenged Brentford to cause a "real surprise" and push for a top two finish in the Premier League this season.
articles.headlineJa: ママドゥ・サンガレ、ブレントフォードにプレミアリーグ「2位以内」への挑戦を促す
articles.descriptionJa: ママドゥ・サンガレは、今シーズンのプレミアリーグで「真のサプライズ」を起こし、2位以内でのフィニッシュを目指すようブレントフォードに求めた。
articles.body:
Mamadou Sangare has challenged Brentford to cause a "real surprise" and push for a top two finish in the Premier League this season.

The Bees are currently fourth in the table after six matches, five points behind second-place Arsenal. They are yet to taste defeat this season, and have picked up eye-catching wins over Tottenham and Chelsea.

The west London club, who were promoted to the Premier League for the first time in 2021, have defied the odds to firmly establish themselves in the top flight.

Despite the departure of long-term boss Thomas Frank last season, they finished ninth and only narrowly missed out on qualifying for Europe for the first time in their history.

Brentford's rise has been built on the back of their refined scouting abilities, through which they spot and develop players that go under the radar of other clubs. Sangare, who signed from Lens this summer on a club-record deal, appears to be the next player in this pipeline.

The midfielder has caught the eye with his tough-tackling performances this season. Like him, the club have begun the season strongly and Sangare feels they are ready to take the next step in their ascent.

"The goal is to reach Europe and win as many games as possible," he said in an interview to Sky Sports.

"We know that Brentford has never played a European game before.

"Why can't we also reach the top four, or the top two? Why can't we cause a real surprise? Because we're a good team in the league. We have a very good team with very good players, with a great coach as well."

- Ranking the top 10 Premier League summer transfers so far

- Premier League overreactions: Takeaways from first games post-international break

A host of elite clubs were in the market for a deep-lying midfielder this summer and Sangare's start for Brenford has raised questions over how he was overlooked by them.

However, the 24-year-old has said he received approaches for other clubs but spurned them in favour of the Bees.

"Yeah it's true [interest from big European clubs]," he said.

"But I'm not going to give any names, out of respect.

"There were a lot of clubs. For me, the most important thing was to know where I could progress. And Brentford was the best place for my development.

"But I'm not going to give any names, out of respect.

"There were a lot of clubs. For me, the most important thing was to know where I could progress. And Brentford was the best place for my development.

"A coach who really wanted me was something that was important to me. That's why I chose Brentford."

articles.headline: Tyler, The Creator to be the next star on Barcelona's shirt
articles.description: American rapper Tyler, The Creator will become the latest artist to feature on the front of Barcelona's jersey when they face Real Madrid in the upcoming Clásico.
articles.headlineJa: タイラー・ザ・クリエイターがバルサのユニフォームを飾る次のスターに
articles.descriptionJa: 次回のエル・クラシコでレアル・マドリードと対戦する際、アメリカ人ラッパーのタイラー・ザ・クリエイターが、バルセロナのユニフォームのフロントに登場する最新のアーティストとなる。
articles.body:
American rapper Tyler, The Creator will become the latest artist to feature on the front of Barcelona's jersey when they face Real Madrid in the upcoming Clásico on Oct. 25.

The special-edition shirt will see the GOLF logo replace Spotify branding on Barça's kit, marking the ninth artist takeover under the club's sponsorship deal with Spotify.

The jersey will also be worn by Barça's women's team against Granada on Oct. 24, with 1,899 limited-edition shirts available to buy -- a nod to the club's founding year.

The GOLF logo represents GOLF WANG, the streetwear and fashion brand founded by Tyler in 2011.

The partnership will also extend beyond the pitch, with Barça and GOLF WANG releasing a special collection featuring jackets, hoodies, track pants, T-shirts, shorts, scarves, socks and more.

The Grammy Award-winning artist recently released the singles "SAG HARBOR" and "THAT GUY," following his 2025 album DON'T TAP THE GLASS.

Both Barça and Madrid both have one more LaLiga fixture before their Oct. 25 meeting at Spotify Camp Nou.

- Tyler, The Creator joins list of music stars to appear on Barcelona's Clásico kit

- Lamine Yamal: Assist for Anthony Gordon in Barcelona win 'almost-rabona'

- Flick urges caution as Barcelona extend perfect start with Champions League win

Hansi Flick's Barcelona travel to Real Betis on Saturday, while José Mourinho's Madrid host Sevilla the following day.

Spanish champions Barça have made a perfect start to their league campaign, winning all eight matches to open a five-point lead over Atlético Madrid and Betis.

Madrid, meanwhile, are six points behind after losing two of their first eight LaLiga games under Mourinho.

articles.headline: Man City's Antoine Semenyo on missed chances against PSG: 'Beating myself up'
articles.description: Antoine Semenyo expressed his frustration over his missed chances in Manchester City's defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: マンシティのアントワン・セメニョ、PSG戦での決定機逸失に「自分を責めている」
articles.descriptionJa: アントワン・セメニョは、水曜日のチャンピオンズリーグでマンチェスター・シティがパリ・サンジェルマンに敗れた試合での決定機を逃したことへの悔しさを表明した。
articles.body:
Antoine Semenyo expressed his frustration over his missed chances in Manchester City's defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The European champions raced into a 3-0 lead in just over 30 minutes at the Etihad to stun the hosts before an improved second-half showing led by Erling Haaland saw the game eventually end 4-2 to PSG.

City pushed PSG hard for a way back, racking up 27 shots and a xG of 2.5. However, their finishing was wayward, with Semenyo especially wasteful. He had an xG of 0.45 and missed a gilt-edged chance soon after Haaland's first goal that would have made the score 3-2.

"It's quite frustrating, to be honest. I think I'm beating myself up a little bit at the moment from all the chances that I missed," Semenyo said in a post-match interview to CBS.

"But I think collectively it was just the reaction and we did so well, caused so many problems. So just unfortunate not to score. So we just take the positives and go again."

PSG's credentials as Europe's best team were again underlined in a scintillating attacking performance at the Etihad, and they look well placed to win a third-successive Champions League title.

They condemned City to their first defeat of the season in all competitions and could have put five goals past them had it not been for Ferran Torres' penalty-miss towards the end.

- Man City can't compete with PSG, the Champions League's gold standard

- Halftime lead worried Luis Enrique in game PSG 'could have lost' to City

"They're one of the best obviously ... Ballon d'Or candidates all around in their team," Semenyo said.

"They made it very hard for us today. We knew what to expect, very unorthodox, credit to them. That's why they're back-to-back European champions."

articles.headline: Why does Haaland score so many goals? Because he's elite at staying onside
articles.description: We know what a dominant scorer Erling Haaland is, but it often goes unnoticed how good he is at avoiding a striker's worst enemy: the offside trap.
articles.body:
The referees are sorry; they really are. According to the Premier League's official statement, the reason VAR overlooked an extremely offside Enzo Fernández on the goal that decided last month's Manchester derby was that officials were simply too busy watching Erling Haaland.

And honestly: who could blame them? The man is captivating in slow mo.

As Josko Gvardiol scooted up the opposite side of the box, Haaland adjusted each stride to stay perfectly level with the ball: a half-step with his left foot, then a lunge with his right, always landing precisely where he needed to be. When Gvardiol curled the cross around Patrick Dorgu some 30 yards away, Haaland was, as best modern technology can measure, three centimeters behind the line of Dorgu's big toe.

Attackers with a special knack for staying onside often don't get as much love as they deserve. The most famous was probably AC Milan striker Filippo Inzaghi, whose high-wire style of play inspired Manchester United boss Sir Alex Ferguson to joke that the "lad must have been born offside."

Inzaghi took that personally. "Thankfully I was born a meter onside," he shot back, "otherwise I wouldn't have scored most of my goals."

Is it possible to measure who's really good or bad at staying onside -- and how much that skill is worth?

For an ability that can decide games or even titles, it's a little strange that we've never had an objective way to separate the Enzos and Haalands of the world. We obsess over players' goals and expected goals, but we rarely stop to wonder how many of those chances come from simply knowing how to stay on the right side of an invisible line.

One easy way to come at this missing measurement might be to count up a player's offside flags, but knowing that Haaland has been caught offside 25 times in the Premier League doesn't really tell us whether he's better or worse at it than Crystal Palace winger Ismaïla Sarr, who has the same number. Stats that aim to measure a skill need to account for the different levels of opportunity players have to do that thing.

So okay, fine, what about comparing offside flags to goals scored?

Now we might be getting somewhere. It's not exactly news that Haaland is a chart-warping statistical freak who piles up goals, but it's pretty mind-boggling to see that he's put up those numbers while being offside slightly less than Nottingham Forest wing back Daniel Muñoz.

What about the rest of the league, though? It's tough to say just from eyeballing this plot whether Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta or Newcastle's Yoane Wissa is better at curving his runs. Trying to use a simple ratio of flags per goal doesn't really work, either. Midfielder Jorginho scored 21 goals for Chelsea and Arsenal while being offside exactly zero times, causing a calculator error that sounds impressive until you try to remember the last time you saw the flag go up on a penalty.

A better way to measure onside skill is to use detailed data on every touch of the ball. Witho

articles.headline: Spurs debut three-guard lineup of Fox, Harper, Castle in preseason win
articles.description: Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed the three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle in a 123-103 preseason win over the Suns on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: スパーズ、プレシーズン戦の勝利でフォックス、ハーパー、キャスルの3ガード体制を初披露
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日のサンズ戦で123-103と勝利したスパーズのミッチ・ジョンソン監督は、ついにディアロン・フォックス、ディラン・ハーパー、ステフォン・キャッスルを起用した3ガード体制を導入した。
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed a three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle in a 123-103 preseason win over the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, explaining "it's time to push forward appropriately" the team's "natural evolution that will still take time."

That was apparent in the group's choppy start as Harper and Castle combined to miss their first five shots before Fox, making his preseason debut, subbed out with 6:57 left in the opening quarter.

But by the time the buzzer sounded for intermission, Fox, Harper and Castle had combined for 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in helping San Antonio seize a 60-49 halftime lead.

"I'm glad they got to play some together and we got some reps out there," Johnson said. "I thought we started the game with some very sloppy possessions, and everybody will have to have a better start to games and a better approach with that."

Fox drilled a corner 3-pointer with one second left for the Spurs' final points of the first half. Castle led all scorers with a game-high 18 points, including 14 from the free throw line. Harper, who finished with nine points, drew the most raucous cheers from the Frost Bank Center crowd with 34.5 seconds left in the second quarter, when he caught a Devin Vassell miss for a rim-rocking tip dunk.

Fox even slammed home a poster dunk in the first half.

"I felt like we were trying to do the right things at the beginning, but we scored so few points," Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama said. "When it clicked, it clicked. The biggest thing is I've got handlers all around me, guys that we want to put the ball in their hands and pick and roll around me. That makes things easier."

Fox, Harper and Castle spent a total of 11 minutes on the court together in the opening half, combining for 19 points to finish with a net rating of plus-10. Fox, Harper and Castle played only 69 minutes together all of last season, including 25 in the NBA Finals, and opponents outscored the Spurs by 47 points in those minutes.

By comparison, the Spurs finished with a plus-9.4 net rating when Fox and Castle shared the court in the regular season, plus-6.2 with Fox and Harper, and plus-11.0 with Harper and Castle.

Fox said the guards spoke over the summer in France, when they visited Wembanyama, about the prospect of potentially playing in the starting lineup together.

"Obviously, when we were in the Finals, and just throughout the playoffs, there were times where we all three played together, a lot more than we did throughout the regular season," Fox said. "But we knew there was a chance that we'd all be starting or at least sharing the court together. We're all excited for it."

articles.headline: Tyler Shough, Kellen Moore respond to criticism from Saints owner Gayle Benson
articles.description: Tyler Shough said Wednesday that he shares the same frustrations of owner Gayle Benson, who a day earlier called the Saints' 1-4 start "unacceptable."
articles.headlineJa: タイラー・ショーとケレン・ムーア、セインツのゲイル・ベンソンオーナーによる批判に反応
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日、タイラー・ショーは、前日にセインツの1勝4敗というスタートを「受け入れられない」と述べたゲイル・ベンソンオーナーと同じ不満を抱いていると語った。
articles.body:
METAIRIE, La. -- New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough said Wednesday that he shares the same frustrations of owner Gayle Benson, who a day earlier called the team's 1-4 start "unacceptable."

"She wasn't saying anything that wasn't already known, and she did a really good job of highlighting the expectations, and we have those same expectations for ourselves," he said.

Benson, in a rare public criticism of her team, told the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club that she won't make excuses for the Saints' play or "accept this level of performance as our standard."

Shough said members of the team saw what Benson said -- "I mean, you obviously see it. It's all over social media" -- but noted the comments won't change their daily process.

"We can't let it regardless, because we win a game and you're the greatest people ever, and you lose some games and it's the worst thing ever," Shough said. "So I've said it before: We're going to have a really good chance to go on a run here. I think it starts with controlling what we can and all of a sudden the narrative changes, or not and we continue to slip and we've got to find a way to control that."

Benson cited shared blame between Saints coach Kellen Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis for the team's struggles.

Moore said Wednesday that he had not met with Benson to discuss what she said. When asked if he took her comments as a declaration that the team needs to show better results soon, he added: "I just think it's where we're at."

"We're 1-4," he said. "We missed a few opportunities right there. ... We all want the same thing. And so we're all shooting for that. We all got the same objectives and we just got to get better moving forward.

"We got great guys in this building that are doing everything they can to find the formula, and all we can control is moving forward as far as playing better, coaching better, giving ourselves the opportunities moving forward. And so I think our guys have the right mindset against the NFL. There's ups and there's downs, and it's about navigating those and getting better moving forward."

The Saints visit the New York Giants (3-1-1) on Sunday.

articles.headline: Love (ankle) sits out Cardinals practice as LaFleur says rest 'vital'
articles.description: Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love didn't practice Wednesday to rest his ailing left ankle. His status for Sunday's game against the Rams isn't clear.
articles.headlineJa: ラフル監督が「休息が不可欠」とし、ラブ（足首）がカージナルスの練習を欠席
articles.descriptionJa: アリゾナ・カージナルスのランニングバック、ジェレマイア・ラブは、左足首の負傷を休ませるため水曜日の練習を休みました。日曜日のラムズ戦への出場可否は不透明です。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice Wednesday to rest his ailing left ankle and his status for Sunday's game against the Rams isn't clear as of yet, coach Mike LaFleur said.

The plan, LaFleur said, is to take Love's ankle "one day at a time," but the Cardinals understand for it to fully heal, the third-overall pick needs to stay off it.

"We all are in agreeance as much as he wants to battle through, we're all in agreeance right now, it's just, hey just give it a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that'll entail for Sunday."

Love's style of play, however, makes it difficult for him to prevent the injury from lingering, LaFleur intimated.

"I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this, too," LaFleur said, "but he's a tough dude. "

But you guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. And, I mean, imagine being a back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you're capable of?"

Asked whether he was concerned about Love's injury lingering, LaFleur swiftly pointed out which body part was injured.

"They're ankles. It's an ankle," LaFleur said. "So, you don't know. I'm not a doctor and each body's a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. I mean, he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it's just lingered."

Love has rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries this season for an average of 3.7 yards per carry. He's also contributed 36 receiving yards and a touchdown on 11 catches. His best game to date came in Week 3 at San Francisco, when he ran for 89 yards.

The Notre Dame star rushed for just 22 yards in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions on 12 carries.

LaFleur said, in some ways, Love's explosiveness has been affected by the ankle injury in recent weeks.

"You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur said. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So, I mean, I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again, the rest for him is going to be vital."
